elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B): "M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against"; "Customer" is defined as Tri City National Bank "(including its Affiliates, 'Customer')", so the defence duty runs to affiliates by definition.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B)(i)-(ii) indemnify Customer (definitionally inclusive of Affiliates) against "any claim by a third party" regarding infringement and M&I services/systems.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B)(i) is limited to "any United States patent, copyright or trademark" — it omits trade-secret misappropriation and non-U.S. IP rights, so it is not a full IP-rights indemnity at the preferred standard. Repair: broaden clause (i) to "any intellectual property right" without the U.S.-only and patent/copyright/trademark-only qualifiers.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B)(iv) is confined to "laws or regulations for the protection of persons or members of a protected class"; no general limb for M&I's breach of applicable law. Repair: add a limb for "M&I's breach of applicable law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb in § 14.2(B) addresses unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data; clause (vii) reaches only tangible property damage or financial loss. Repair: add a limb for unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by M&I.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B) contains no gross negligence / wilful misconduct limb; clause (vii) covers only property damage or financial loss from acts or omissions. Repair: add an express "M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct" limb.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: § 14.3: "such indemnitee shall give notice of such claim to the indemnifying party, including a brief description of the amount and basis therefor".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: § 14.3: indemnifying party "shall be entitled to assume control of the defense of the claim with counsel chosen by the indemnifying party, reasonably satisfactory to the indemnitee".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: § 14.3: "Indemnitee shall cooperate fully with, and assist, the indemnifying party in its defense ... in all reasonable respects".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(A) extends to Customer's inaccurate reps/warranties, harassment, work-related injury or death, tangible property and financial loss, and § 6.6(B) matters — far broader than Customer content plus breach of law, and the redline leaves it unchanged. Repair: narrow § 14.2(A) to Customer-provided content and Customer's violation of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: § 14.2(B)(i): indemnity and defence for "any claim by a third party that the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark" — an IP indemnity at the fallback standard (which tolerates usual qualifications).

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; its condition does not apply. § 14.2(B)(i) takes no Customer-modification exclusion, which is more favourable to us, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; condition not applicable. No combination carve-out appears in § 14.2(B)(i) and none was inserted — unqualified scope favours Customer.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; condition not applicable. No Customer-specification exclusion exists or was added; the indemnity remains unqualified.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: New § 14.2 C: "M&I shall procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected Services or software, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing."

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: New § 14.2 C: "If none of those remedies is available, M&I shall refund to Customer the fees paid for the affected Services or software." Obligation is unconditional on failure of the other remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: § 13.4 as amended: "except that M&I's liability for its indemnification obligations under Section 14.2(B) shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid to M&I by Customer under this Agreement" — replaces the three-month cap for the indemnity with exactly 3× annual fees.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the pre-existing § 14.2(B)(i) IP indemnity with defence duty and § 14.3 notice/control/cooperation procedures survive, the redline supplies the missing procure/modify/replace continuity remedy with a fee refund, and it carves the § 14.2(B) indemnity out of the three-month cap at exactly 3× annual fees.

Preferred level is not reached: no general breach-of-applicable-law limb, no Customer Data breach limb, no gross negligence/wilful misconduct limb, clause (i) is confined to U.S. patent/copyright/trademark rather than all IP rights, and Customer's § 14.2(A) indemnity remains far broader than Customer-provided content plus Customer's breach of law. Correctly not pressed given the fallback target.

Minimality holds: only two operations (insert § 14.2 C; add a cap exception in § 13.4). No favourable existing wording was deleted or paraphrased, the one-year suit limitation and 'notwithstanding any provision' language are retained verbatim, and the insertion carries no extras (no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, added damages categories, or procedural boilerplate) beyond what elements 5-7 require.

Intent is preserved: the general three-month liability cap, § 14.3 procedures, § 14.2(A) and the § 6.6(B) cross-reference all continue to operate without contradiction, and the new § 14.2 C references an existing, defined clause (§ 14.2(B)(i)) so no dangling term is created.

Drafting refinement to consider (not a defect against the checklist): the § 13.4 carve-out names only Section 14.2(B), so the new § 14.2 C refund could still be squeezed by the three-month general cap given the 'Notwithstanding any provision' opener; extending the exception to 'Section 14.2(B) and (C)' would close that gap.
